newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses rise strongly, boosted by Clinton.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses rise strongly, boosted by Clinton.

text.p: European bourses climbed sharply on Wednesday as investors welcomed President Clinton's re-election and the Republicans retaining their grip on Congress as good news for business.

The dollar also strengthened as the American electorate's decision to maintain the status quo was met with relief on foreign exchange markets. But profit-takers later took some of the shine off the U.S. currency.

London, Frankfurt and Paris chalked up strong gains with an optimistic mood building up as the Republican victory in the House and Senate banished earlier doubts and lifted hopes that a lid would be kept on U.S. government spending.
Worries about a Democrat clean sweep had unnerved markets ahead of the election, concerned about what such an outcome might have meant for public spending in Washington.
"The mark-up was on the cards after we got what looks like the ideal outcome to the U.S. election," one dealer said.
In Paris, shares leapt to a year's high at the opening, rallying strongly on the back of Clinton's return for a second term, traders said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up nearly one percent.

The best performer was Frankfurt where floor trading registered a gain of 1.4 percent by mid-morning, helped by the Clinton win, overnight gains on Wall Street and the firmer dollar. London's gains were a more modest 0.3 percent as the early U.S. election momentum was eroded by a Bank of England report that more interest rate hikes could follow last week's surpise increase of 0.25 percentage point.
The British central bank said a further increase in rates was probable in due course as the government was unlikely to meet its 2.5 percent inflation target.

"Even after the recent increase in official interest rates of 1/4 percentage point, it remains more likely than not that inflation will be above the target at the end of the forecast horizon," it said in its quarterly Inflation Report.
Positive reports about heart surgery on Russian President Boris Yeltsin were called "welcome" but of little consequence to the market at present.

On the currency markets, the dollar shed some of its early gains on the mark and yen made as the results confirmed the Republicans had retained control of congress. By midday, it was back to Tuesday's closing levels.
The foreign exchanges were cheered in early transactions by Clinton's win but were clearly relieved his hands will be tied by a Republican Congress, regarded as pro-business.

"The markets are breathing a whole sigh of relief...Clinton has retained the White House and the Republicans have retained their grip on the House (of Representatives)," David Brown, chief economist at Bear Stearns said.

Analysts said the dollar's prospects looked healthy. "Markets believe Clinton will keep a tight rein on the Republican tax cutting agenda, while the Republican Congress will operate to keep his spending priorities in check," Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank said.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5189 marks and 113.98 yen. compared with 1.5188 and 114.05 in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 4.3 points at 3,925.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 18.82 at 2,206.14
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 36.28 at 2,727.57.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $377.90 an ounce, compared to $379.35 at the close on Tuesday. Silver was at $4.80, down four cents.
